title.narrative: Indicator 2: The number of internal audit units of ministries, departments, and agencies (MDAs) and local government authorities (LGAs) that improved their compliance with international standards by one step (Standards of the Institute of Internal Auditors, IIA).

description.narrative: Exante / expost analysis of audit reports of (selected) MDAs/LGAs by independent expert through an assessment tool developed during programme implementation, in accordance with IIA standards. Compliance with international standards in internal audit reports is measured by the gradations nonconformance, partially conformance and general conformance. An improvement of non conformance to partially conformance or of partially conformance to general conformance is considered an improvement. The exante analysis was carried out in 2021. The expost analysis will be carried out in November 2023.

comment.narrative: 0 out of 30 internal audit units conform with international standards. Internal Audit reports in 11 out of 30 internal audit units partially conform with international standards.
Improvement by one step in 17 internal audit units out of 30 IAUs.
The expost analysis will be carried out in November 2023.

description.narrative: Indicator 3: Number of businesses registered for a business license that paid service levy in financial year 2022/23 (in 15 partner LGAs).

comment.narrative: 9373 businesses registered for business license have paid service levy in FY 201920.
12185 businesses increased by 30 percentage points in FY 202223 062023.

At the end of financial year 202223 the monitored 15 LGAs out of 21 which receive support the number of unique service levy payers according to the monitoring exercise conducted by the program amounts to 7.455. This is 1.742 payers 3049 more than in financial year 201920 that was taken as the baseline year. Increase in service levy payers for the complete set of LGAs receiving support is even larger at 6510 or 5.874 new service levy payers.

description.narrative: CLOSED CONTRACT (GFG Phase 1) In 15 partner LGAs, 320 out of 400 participants in a consultation meeting (e.g. dialogue meeting, District Business Council, publicly accessible council meeting, virtual dialogue meeting) perceive an improvement in the dialogue between LGAs and population and rank the improvement on a scale of at least 4 out of 5.Various qualitative aspects of the dialogue will be assessed in the surveys, such as the provision of information to citizens; the ability of citizens to freely express their views and concerns during dialogue meetings; the degree to which citizens feel that their expressed concerns are being taken into account.

comment.narrative: there are no specific consultation mechanism on local tax system tax payer rights and obligations budget plans and execution in LGAs

According to Outcome Indicator 4 reflecting the contribution of Field of Action 4 Social Accountability to the overall objective of the programme in five partner LGAs 23 of 400 participants in a consultation mechanism e.g. representatives of private sector associations CSOs interest groups LGAs perceived an improvement in the dialogue between LGAs and population. At the same time as the delayed rollout of interventions at the local level by FoA 3 FoA 4 conducted scoping missions in all five GFG clusters. ArushaKilimanjaro and Tanga were selected as the most appropriate partner clusters for FoA4 at local level with the possibility of including Kigoma or Morogoro at a later stage. An indepth stakeholder mapping of the two selected clusters resulted in the preliminary choice of Arusha CC Longido DC Tanga CC and Korogwe DC as the first partner LGAs for FoA4. A fifth and possibly sixth partner LGA will be selected in the near future.PFB02 GFG Narrative ReportFin bottom pg

description.narrative: CLOSED CONTRACT (GFG Phase I). The updated audit manual for revenue audits is applied in the audits of FY 2016/17 and 2017/18.

comment.narrative: Output Indicator A2 concerns the updating and subsequent application of the revenue audit manual. The specialized audit manual which is currently in use was developed under the previous German support programme with NAOT. In view of the key functions of Bank of Tanzania and the level of risk involved if they are not carried out properly creating an Audit Manual for BoT covering both compliance aspects and financial auditing took priority. As a result the update for revenue audits was postponed to 2018 which means that the possible number of applied audits has been reduced to one instead of two FYs until 2020. Output Indicator A2 has therefore been adjusted as follows the updated audit manual for revenue audits is applied in the audit of FY 201819. In order to compensate for the reduction in applied audits and to reflect the relevant work regarding BoT audits a new indicator A4 is defined a specialized audit manual for the Bank of Tanzania is applied by NAOT for the audits of the FY 201718 and 201819. PFB02 GFG Narrative ReportFin pg 1630 1st para.

comment.narrative: Output Indicator A2 concerns the updating and subsequent application of the revenue audit manual. The specialized audit manual which is currently in use was developed under the previous German support programme with NAOT. In view of the key functions of Bank of Tanzania and the level of risk involved if they are not carried out properly creating an Audit Manual for BoT covering both compliance aspects and financial auditing took priority. As a result the update for revenue audits was postponed to 2018 which means that the possible number of applied audits has been reduced to one instead of two FYs until 2020. Output Indicator A2 has therefore been adjusted as follows the updated audit manual for revenue audits is applied in the audit of FY 201819. In order to compensate for the reduction in applied audits and to reflect the relevant work regarding BoT audits a new indicator A4 is defined a specialized audit manual for the Bank of Tanzania is applied by NAOT for the audits of the FY 201718 and 201819.
